title: [Pre-Phase 1] Scaffold solution structure (Api, Web, Core, Data, Mobile)
body:
## Goal
Create the target project boundary from architecture-design §1 without changing the deployed save path.

## Depends on
- None. This can start immediately.

## Steps
1. Add `net10.0` projects and include them in `ReMind.sln` under the existing `src` and `tests` solution folders: `src/ReMind.Api` (ASP.NET Core Web API), `src/ReMind.Core` (class library), `src/ReMind.Data` (class library), `src/ReMind.Web` (React + TypeScript; Vite is the default toolchain), `src/ReMind.Mobile` (Expo React Native placeholder), `tests/ReMind.IntegrationTests` (xUnit, references Api/Data).
2. Api references Core and Data. Data references Core. Unit tests keep compiling against the current Frontend and Functions projects and may also reference Core.
3. Web has `npm run build` and `npm test` (a passing placeholder test is enough). Mobile has a TypeScript check and a Jest placeholder. Neither calls Azure.
4. Api starts and exposes only a stub; do not register JWT, EF, or a public business route yet. Data contains an empty `ReMindDbContext` class with no migration.
5. Do not delete `src/ReMind.Frontend`, `src/ReMind.Functions`, or `database/ReMind.Database`. Do not change `deploy-solution` publish paths in this issue.
6. Update the root README target-structure note to point at §1 and `docs/operations-setup.md`. State that Razor and Functions HTTP remain until cutover.

## Contracts and invariants
- Public HTTP remains Functions + function key until the cutover issue. Workers are not a second public API.
- Schema source of truth is not switched in this issue.
- Mobile feature parity is Phase 4. This issue only reserves the project.

## Tests
- `dotnet build ReMind.sln` and `dotnet test ReMind.sln` stay green, including the existing Playwright save-workflow tests.
- `npm ci && npm test && npm run build` in `src/ReMind.Web`.
- Mobile `tsc --noEmit` (or the Expo equivalent) succeeds.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Solution layout matches the §1 tree, including `tests/ReMind.IntegrationTests`.
- [ ] Current Razor/Functions save path and Playwright harness still pass.
- [ ] README names the retirement plan and does not claim the new apps are deployed.

## Out of scope
- EF migrations
- Entra tenant
- Terraform SKU changes
- Deleting Razor or Functions

## References
- `docs/architecture-design.md` §1 and §13 Pre-Phase 1
- `ReMind.sln`

## Implementation rules
- Contract: `docs/architecture-design.md`. If this issue disagrees with the doc, follow the doc and record the drift in the PR.
- Put Azure resources in `infra/terraform` (`hashicorp/azurerm` `~> 4.0`). Portal or `az` steps are only the exceptions in `docs/operations-setup.md`.

## Goal
Stop deploying schema from `ReMind.Database` before the first EF-backed database deployment, and prove whether any environment already has rows.

## Depends on
- [Pre-Phase 1] Scaffold solution structure (Api, Web, Core, Data, Mobile)

## Steps
1. Remove `azure/sql-action` from `.github/workflows/deploy-database.yml`. Delete the workflow if nothing else remains, and remove any other CI path that builds or publishes `database/ReMind.Database`.
2. Keep the SQL project files in git only as a reference. They must not be a deploy input. Say that explicitly in the README.
3. Inventory every shared, dev, and prod database that may have run Functions or `deploy-database`. Run the query in `docs/operations-setup.md` §2. Write the result (server, row count, whether `Location` is `NVARCHAR`) in the PR. If you cannot reach an environment, stop and say which secret or firewall blocked you. Do not guess greenfield.
4. If any `dbo.DataPoints` row exists, do not add a drop/rename script. Open the disposition notes (NVARCHAR location, missing `UserId`/`Title`, rollback) and block the EF migration issue.
5. Remove the GitHub secret `AZURE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING` from the documented required set once the workflow no longer reads it. Do not print the secret while confirming it is unused.
6. Do not add a SQL firewall rule, and do not enable Allow Azure services, to finish this inventory. Use an existing operator path or record the inventory as blocked.

## Contracts and invariants
- EF migrations in `ReMind.Data` are the only future schema apply path.
- A crash or missing inventory is not permission to apply a new schema over live rows.

Follow `docs/operations-setup.md` §1.7 and §2. `deploy-database` cannot reach SQL from a GitHub-hosted runner unless a temporary named-IP firewall rule already exists. Do not add `0.0.0.0`.

- `dotnet test` still passes. This issue does not need a new SQL test.

- [ ] Deploy and CI no longer apply `database/ReMind.Database`.
- [ ] Inventory result is in the PR, or the PR stops with the exact access gap.
- [ ] No EF migration is applied to a database that still has legacy rows.

title: [Phase 1] Entra External ID tenant + app registrations (API, SPA, Mobile, Admin role)
body:
## Goal
Stand up Microsoft Entra External ID as the only customer identity provider, with API, SPA, and mobile clients plus an Admin role.

## Depends on
- None. This can start immediately.

## Steps
1. Create the External ID tenant manually, in a different directory from the SQL server Entra tenant. Record tenant id and primary domain in the PR (ids only).
2. Grant the GitHub deployment identity application administrator in that tenant if policy allows, then add an `azuread` provider alias in `infra/terraform` scoped to the External ID tenant.
3. Terraform the three app registrations: API (exposed scope and audience), SPA (authorization code + PKCE, local and deployed redirect URIs), mobile public client (PKCE, redirect scheme chosen by the mobile scaffold). No client secret on the SPA or mobile app.
4. Terraform an app role whose token claim is `roles` containing `Admin`. Document that assignment is Entra-only. Do not add a self-service role API.
5. Configure Google, Apple, and Facebook as External ID identity providers. Create the vendor apps in those consoles (manual). Store client secrets in GitHub environment secrets and write them to Key Vault with Terraform. Do not commit secrets.
6. Output tenant id, API audience, and the three client ids as non-secret Terraform outputs for later app settings.
7. If the deployment identity cannot be added to the External ID tenant, stop after the tenant exists, write the portal click list into the PR, and do not pretend the apps are IaC.

## Contracts and invariants
- Admin claim format is `roles` contains `Admin` (§8).
- Customer tokens are not issued by the SQL server's Entra tenant.
- SPA and mobile use PKCE. Resource-owner password and implicit flow are out.

## Manual setup
Follow `docs/operations-setup.md` §3 for the tenant, social consoles, and secret names. App registrations and the Admin role are Terraform unless that section's exception applies.

## Tests
- A non-prod user can complete auth-code + PKCE against the SPA app and receive a token whose audience is the API app.
- An operator assigned the app role receives `roles: Admin`. An ordinary user does not.
- `terraform validate` passes. No secret appears in the plan output.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Runbook and Terraform outputs cover tenant, three apps, and Admin role.
- [ ] Social IdP client secrets exist only in Key Vault / GitHub secrets.
- [ ] Token audience matches what `ReMind.Api` will validate.

## Out of scope

title: [Phase 1] EF Core model + initial transactional migration for full §2 schema
body:
## Goal
Materialize every §2 table in `ReMind.Data` with one transactional initial migration and no spatial index.

## Depends on
- [Pre-Phase 1] Scaffold solution structure (Api, Web, Core, Data, Mobile)
- [Pre-Phase 1] Retire ReMind.Database as schema source of truth

## Steps
1. Add entities and `IEntityTypeConfiguration` for Users, AvatarUploads, DataPointChains, DataPoints, Tags, DataPointTags, UserConsents, GpsFixes, ErasedSubjectHashes, UserErasureRequests, UserExportRequests, Media, OutboxMessages, Follows, Comments, Reactions, and Reports. Column nullability, lengths, defaults, checks, and filtered indexes match the §2 DDL, not a subset.
2. Map `DataPoints.Location` and `GpsFixes.Location` to `geography` with SRID 4326. Configure the SRID check. Do not emit `CREATE SPATIAL INDEX` in this migration.
3. Add global query filters `!IsDeleted` on DataPoints and Comments. Document that admin queries must use `IgnoreQueryFilters()` explicitly.
4. Seed, in the migration or a hosted seeder that is idempotent on the unique key: system tags from `src/ReMind.Data/Seeding/system-tags.json`, and one non-authenticating tombstone user. The tombstone has a fixed GUID in code, no Issuer/ExternalSubject that a token can match, and is not returned by profile search. List the starter tag names in the PR for product confirmation; they are data, not a schema decision. Suggested starter set: Historic site, Conflict, Culture, Industry, Transport, Disaster.
5. Generate the initial migration with `dotnet ef` from `ReMind.Data`. Inspect the SQL: tables, FKs, checks, filtered unique indexes (`UQ_AvatarUploads_OneLivePerOwner`, chain/user/media indexes) are present; `CREATE SPATIAL INDEX` is absent. The migration must apply on an empty database and be safe to retry after a failed transaction.
6. Do not apply this migration to a shared database in this issue. Local/Testcontainers only, and only after the retire issue recorded an empty inventory or this PR is explicitly greenfield.
7. Pin `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer.NetTopologySuite` to a current 10.x build compatible with `net10.0`.

## Contracts and invariants
- `Users` has no `AvatarUploadId` column. Live avatar state is `AvatarUploads` plus `PendingReservedBytes`.
- `Visibility` has no database default.
- `ErasedSubjectHashes.SubjectHash` is `binary(32)` plus `KeyVersion`. Do not store a plain SHA-256 of the subject.
- Comments parent FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Same-DataPointId is enforced in the write transaction later, not by a cross-table check that EF cannot express unless you add a composite key design that still matches §2.
- Follows check rejects self-follow. Reports check requires exactly one target.

## Tests
- Integration test applies the migration to Testcontainers SQL Server and inserts one legal row per table.
- Tests expect check failures for negative `PendingReservedBytes`, visibility outside 0-2, self-follow, and a report with both targets set.
- A second apply of the same migration on a database that already has the history row is a no-op.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Model covers every §2 column in the DDL and the supporting-table notes.
- [ ] Initial migration is transactional and contains no spatial index.
- [ ] Soft-delete filters are on by default.
- [ ] Tombstone user and system-tag seed are idempotent.

## Out of scope
- Spatial index DDL
- API endpoints
- Applying the migration to production

title: [Phase 1] ReMind.Api foundation: JWT auth, fallback policy, Problem Details, EF+NTS
body:
## Goal
Stand up `ReMind.Api` as the only future public HTTP API, with secure defaults and no business endpoints yet.

## Depends on
- [Pre-Phase 1] Scaffold solution structure (Api, Web, Core, Data, Mobile)
- [Phase 1] EF Core model + initial transactional migration for full §2 schema

## Steps
1. Reference `Microsoft.Identity.Web` (current 3.x/4.x compatible with `net10.0`) and call `AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi` from the `AzureAd` configuration section. Do not hand-roll JWT validation.
2. Set `FallbackPolicy` to `RequireAuthenticatedUser`. Call `UseAuthentication` and `UseAuthorization` before `MapControllers`. Swagger UI may be Development-only; the OpenAPI document itself is generated in all environments.
3. Mark only `GET /healthz/live` anonymous in this issue. The erasure status route is added later and is the other anonymous exception. `/healthz/live` returns 200 with no body that contains user data, and it must not resolve a user or JIT a profile.
4. Add `ApiProblems` in `ReMind.Api` (stable `type` and `code` extension) writing `application/problem+json` for 400/401/403/404/409/429. Do not include stack traces or SQL errors. Seed codes used later: `validation.failed`, `auth.unauthorized`, `auth.forbidden`, `account-closed`, `resource.not-found`, `quota-exceeded`.
5. Register `ReMindDbContext` with `UseSqlServer` + `UseNetTopologySuite`. Local config may use a developer connection string from user-secrets. Deployed config must be a managed-identity / Key Vault reference owned by the Terraform issues, not a password checked into appsettings.json.
6. Add CORS policy that reads an explicit origin allow-list. Reject `*` and reject `AllowAnyOrigin` combined with credentials.
7. Add rate-limiter services with no endpoint policies yet, so later issues can attach named policies. Forwarded headers only from the Front Door hop, configured when the Front Door issue lands; do not trust `X-Forwarded-For` from arbitrary clients in the meantime.
8. Publish OpenAPI including the bearer scheme. Document `AzureAd` keys: Instance, TenantId, ClientId, Audience. Values come from the Entra issue outputs. Placeholders are allowed until that issue merges, but the middleware must still reject missing tokens.

## Contracts and invariants
- Anonymous is never the default.
- Health probe path is `GET /healthz/live`, not `/healthz` and not `/api/health`.
- Problem Details `code` values are stable strings, not HTTP status numbers.

## Tests
- WebApplicationFactory: GET a non-health route without a token returns 401 problem+json.
- `GET /healthz/live` returns 200 without a token and does not touch `Users`.
- A sample validation result uses `ApiProblems` and does not contain an exception message from a thrown SQL exception.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Protected routes require a token.
- [ ] Health probe is anonymous and side-effect free.
- [ ] DbContext resolves with NTS geography mapping in a Testcontainers or skipped-if-no-docker integration test.

## Out of scope
- Business controllers
- Data Protection key ring
- Front Door access restrictions

title: [Phase 1] Caller identity directory + JIT user provisioning with erasure blocklist
body:
## Goal
Resolve `Users.UserId` only from the validated token, and refuse JIT when the subject was erased.

## Depends on
- [Phase 1] ReMind.Api foundation: JWT auth, fallback policy, Problem Details, EF+NTS
- [Phase 1] EF Core model + initial transactional migration for full §2 schema

## Steps
1. Add `IUserDirectory.GetCurrentUserIdAsync(ClaimsPrincipal, CancellationToken)` used by every later controller. Read `iss` plus `oid`. If `oid` is absent, read the one explicitly configured linked-subject claim and fail closed if that claim is also absent. Never read `userId` from query, route, or body for the caller.
2. Add `ISubjectPseudonymKeyRing` that returns the current key version and every version still present in `ErasedSubjectHashes.KeyVersion`. Production implementation reads Key Vault (`docs/operations-setup.md` §5). Tests use an in-memory ring.
3. On first authenticated request, compute `HMAC-SHA-256(key[v], UTF8(issuer) || 0x00 || UTF8(externalSubject))` for each loaded version. If any hash matches `SubjectHash` for that `KeyVersion`, return 403 `account-closed` and do not insert a user.
4. Otherwise insert `Users` in a transaction that tolerates a concurrent insert on `UQ_Users_Issuer_ExternalSubject` by re-reading the winner. Display name comes from a token name claim or a generated placeholder; it is not a client-supplied id.
5. Do not run this pipeline from `/healthz/live` or from the later erasure-status route.
6. Add an authorization requirement that a resolved user exists for normal routes, so a closed account cannot fall through to an empty guid.

## Contracts and invariants
- Plain SHA-256 of the subject is not acceptable.
- Key versions referenced by the blocklist must be loaded even if they are outside a rotation window.
- Client-supplied user ids are ignored for authorization.

## Manual setup
Key material is created per `docs/operations-setup.md` §5. This issue may ship the Key Vault reader before the vault exists if configuration fails closed (503 `identity.keys-unavailable`) rather than skipping the blocklist check.

## Tests
- First call creates one user; second call returns the same id.
- Seeded `ErasedSubjectHashes` row for the token subject returns 403 `account-closed` and leaves `Users` unchanged.
- A request body `userId` different from the token does not change the resolved id.
- Concurrent first-login requests produce one row.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] JIT works for a new subject.
- [ ] Erased subject cannot reprovision.
- [ ] No endpoint in this change trusts a client user id.

## Out of scope
- Erasure worker
- Profile edit API
- Disabling Key Vault key versions

## References
- `docs/architecture-design.md` §2 ErasedSubjectHashes, §3 Caller Identity, §12
- `docs/operations-setup.md` §5

title: [Phase 1] Opaque cursor infrastructure (Data Protection, caller-bound, TTL)
body:
## Goal
Provide one opaque cursor implementation for every visibility-dependent list.

## Depends on
- [Phase 1] ReMind.Api foundation: JWT auth, fallback policy, Problem Details, EF+NTS

## Steps
1. Register ASP.NET Data Protection and persist the key ring to Azure Blob or Key Vault via the app identity when `AzureAd`/hosting config says Production. Local dev may use the filesystem key ring. Document the container in the Terraform foundation issue; do not store key-ring files in git.
2. Add `ICursorProtector` with create/redeem. Payload contains `callerUserId`, route name, seek keys, and the bound query inputs for that route. TTL is the §8 cursor TTL (10 minutes) from options, not a hard-coded magic number once the defaults issue exists; until then use 10 minutes and switch to options in that issue.
3. Redeem failures (expired, tampered, caller mismatch, route mismatch, bound-input mismatch) return the same 400 `cursor.invalid` problem. Do not say which field failed.
4. Ship typed payloads for nearby, nearby/gps, chain-candidates, timeline, in-bounds clusters, in-bounds points, place search, feed, comments, and follow-requests, even if the endpoints land later. Empty pages must be able to return a null continuation.

## Contracts and invariants
- Cursors are not OFFSET and not raw JSON in the query string.
- A cursor issued to user A is rejected for user B.
- Nearby seek keys are `(distanceMeters, dataPointId)` and must not be reused for chain candidates.

## Tests
- Unit tests: expiry, tamper, caller mismatch, route mismatch, and bound-input mismatch each yield the same error code.
- Round-trip preserves seek keys and caller id.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Shared protector exists and is registered in DI.
- [ ] Production key ring is not ephemeral per instance.

## Goal
Profile read/update and a quota-safe avatar upload that never trusts a client blob path.

## Depends on
- [Phase 1] Caller identity directory + JIT user provisioning with erasure blocklist

## Steps
1. Implement `GET /api/users/{id}`. Return display name, bio, and a short-lived signed read URL when `AvatarBlobPath` is set. Never return a writable path or the raw blob name as a secret. Unknown ids return the same not-found as a hidden profile if you cannot safely distinguish them; do not 500.
2. `PUT /api/users/me` accepts display name (max 200) and bio (max 1000) only. Reject `AvatarBlobPath`, `avatarUrl`, and any property that looks like a blob path with 400 `validation.failed`.
3. `POST /api/users/me/avatar` accepts `clientRequestId` and `requestedSizeBytes` (photo types only, 1 byte through avatar max). In one transaction: lock the user row, cancel prior non-terminal avatar reservations, release their `PendingReservedBytes` only if they used the size-enforcing proxy or their write SAS is already expired, then debit the photo max (10 MB) with a conditional update. 0-row update is 409 `quota-exceeded`. Persist `AvatarUploads` with staging path `avatars/{userId}/staging/{uploadId}/...` and canonical path `avatars/{userId}/{uploadId}/...`.
4. Idempotent retry of the same live `clientRequestId` returns the same `uploadId`, SAS, and reserved bytes and does not debit again.
5. Prefer the size-enforcing API proxy for the avatar bytes (hard stop at reserved bytes). Direct SAS is allowed only if the media-worker inspector from the workers issue covers avatar staging keys too.
6. `POST /api/users/me/avatar/complete` validates size and signature, seals `CanonicalETag`, and does not set `Users.AvatarBlobPath` until malware verdict is clean for that ETag and signature validation passed. Human moderation is optional for avatars and defaults off. Delete the previous canonical avatar only after the new path is live.
7. Enforce `UQ_AvatarUploads_OneLivePerOwner` in the transaction, not only by catching a unique-index error after a double debit.

## Contracts and invariants
- Client cannot set `AvatarBlobPath`.
- Reserved bytes for an avatar are the type max, not the client-declared size.
- Two concurrent inits cannot leave two live charged reservations.

## Tests
- Integration: concurrent avatar inits produce one live row and one debit.
- Retry returns the same upload id without a second debit.
- PUT with `avatarBlobPath` returns 400 and does not change the column.
- Complete without a clean verdict does not publish the avatar.

Actually linking is the chain issue; this issue may accept the fields and return 400 `chain.not-implemented` until that issue replaces the handler, or it may no-op only if the chain issue is in the same PR. ## Goal
Implement chain create, candidate search, timeline, and the concurrency claims the design requires.

## Depends on

1. `POST /api/chains` creates an empty chain with optional title (max 200) and `CreatedByUserId = caller`.
2. `GET /api/datapoints/chain-candidates` and `/chain-candidates/gps` use the same visibility predicate as nearby (Accepted follows only). GPS route takes `gpsFixId` only. Return chains that have any visible node within radius, plus standalone visible points the caller owns. Sort `(minVisibleDistanceMeters ASC, candidateKind ASC, stableId ASC)` with chain=0 and standalone=1. Cursor seeks `>` on that tuple and binds caller, center or gpsFixId, radius, and page size. Labels and counts use the visible subset only.
3. `GET /api/chains/{chainId}/timeline` orders `EventDate DESC, DataPointId DESC`, visibility-filtered, cursor binds caller and seeks `<` on `(eventDate, dataPointId)`.
4. `POST /api/chains/{chainId}/datapoints` creates a point in the chain. Non-empty chains require a visible node within `associationRadiusMeters`. Empty-chain first node is allowed only for `CreatedByUserId`, and only if a conditional claim updates the chain while no data point references it (0-row update means re-evaluate association against the now-non-empty chain). Two concurrent first-node requests must not both skip proximity.
5. `linkToDataPointId` on create: caller must own that point, it must be standalone, and the update `SET ChainId = @new WHERE DataPointId = @id AND ChainId IS NULL AND UserId = @caller` must affect 1 row in the same transaction as the new point insert. 0 rows is 409 `chain.conflict`. Cross-user invite is not implemented.
6. Joining an existing `chainId` requires the caller can view at least one in-range node, or the empty-chain creator exception above.

## Contracts and invariants
- `chainId` and `linkToDataPointId` together are 400.
- Hidden members never affect labels, counts, or candidate distance.
- Pending follows do not make a FollowersOnly node visible for association.

## Tests
- Integration: two concurrent empty-chain first-node calls; exactly one skips proximity; the loser is checked against the new node.
- Two concurrent `linkToDataPointId` calls against one standalone point produce one chain, not two.
- Timeline cursor from user A is rejected for user B.
- Candidate payload does not include a hidden private node's title.

2. GPS route redeems the fix (consent re-check) and rejects a cursor whose bound `gpsFixId`, radius, route, or caller does not match.

- Client cannot pass `currentUserId`.

- Pending follow excludes a FollowersOnly point. Accepted follow includes it.
- Replaying another user's cursor returns `cursor.invalid`.

title: [Phase 2] Media upload init/complete with PendingReservedBytes quota
body:
## Goal
Author-only data-point media reservation and completion with a conditional quota debit.

## Depends on
- [Phase 2] Data points CRUD with required visibility and ownership rules
- [Phase 2] Operational defaults configuration module (§8 bounds)
- [Infra] Media storage, queues, Event Grid, Defender, RBAC

## Steps
1. `POST /api/datapoints/{id}/media` is author-only (non-authors get shared 404). Body: `clientRequestId`, `requestedSizeBytes`, media type photo or video. `requestedSizeBytes` must be > 0 and ≤ type max (50 MB photo, 500 MB video).
2. Debit `Users.PendingReservedBytes` by the type max, not the client size: `UPDATE Users SET PendingReservedBytes = PendingReservedBytes + @typeMax WHERE UserId = @caller AND PendingReservedBytes + @typeMax <= @quota`. 0 rows is 409 `quota-exceeded`. Do not `SUM(ReservedBytes)` under read committed.
3. Insert `Media` PendingUpload with staging path `media/{userId}/{dataPointId}/staging/{uploadId}/{fileName}` and canonical path `media/{userId}/{dataPointId}/{uploadId}/{fileName}`. Unique `(OwnerUserId, DataPointId, ClientRequestId)`. Retry of a live key returns the same upload id, SAS, and reserved bytes without a second debit.
4. Mint a user-delegation SAS (managed identity, no account key) for that staging blob only, create+write, TTL ≤ pending expiry (15 minutes default, never days).
5. `POST .../media/complete` checks the staging blob size, signature (JPEG/PNG/WebP/MP4/MOV by content, not the client MIME alone), and requested size. Seal by conditional copy of the validated ETag to the canonical path and persist `CanonicalETag`. Transition to Processing or PendingModeration, or Rejected with `RejectedUtc` set in the same statement. Insert one `OutboxMessages` row keyed by upload id + work type only on the first successful pending→processing/pending-moderation transition.
6. Direct-SAS rejection does not release `PendingReservedBytes` until `UploadExpiresUtc` / SAS `se`. Proxy uploads may release immediately. Document which path this endpoint uses. Photos should prefer single-shot `Put Blob`. Chunked SAS is only for large video and only with the worker inspector.
7. Read APIs must not sign non-Ready media. This issue adds the filter even if the list DTO is otherwise empty.

## Contracts and invariants
- Quota charges the type maximum.
- Completion is idempotent. Terminal Ready/Rejected retries do not enqueue a second outbox row.
- `If-None-Match: *` is a client hint, not the security boundary. The boundary is the sealed canonical ETag.

## Tests
- Concurrent inits at the quota boundary: one succeeds, one returns `quota-exceeded`.
- Retry does not double-debit.
- Complete twice inserts one outbox row.
- Non-author receives 404.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-Ready media is absent from read DTOs.

title: [Phase 2] Media workers: outbox dispatcher, malware scan, thumbnails, cleanup janitors
body:
## Goal
Background pipeline that reaches Ready only after clean scan, thumbnail, and moderation gates match the sealed ETag.

## Depends on
- [Phase 2] Media upload init/complete with PendingReservedBytes quota
- [Infra] Media storage, queues, Event Grid, Defender, RBAC

## Steps
1. Implement workers in `ReMind.Functions` as queue/timer triggers only. Do not add HTTP triggers. Remove is not required yet; do not expand the existing public save function.
2. Outbox dispatcher polls `IX_OutboxMessages_Unprocessed`, publishes at-least-once, and sets `ProcessedUtc` after ack. `DedupKey` prevents duplicate work rows. Crash between commit and publish must be recovered by the next poll.
3. Scan-result worker consumes Defender/Event Grid events. Persist `MalwareScanVerdict` and `MalwareScannedUtc` only when blob path, upload id, and `CanonicalETag` match. Ignore stale ETags. Timeout/error leaves the row non-Ready (`Quarantined` with `QuarantineReviewByUtc`, or the design's Error/Timeout verdict). Never parse with ImageSharp or FFmpeg unless verdict is Clean for that ETag.
4. Thumbnail worker writes `media/{userId}/{dataPointId}/thumbnails/{uploadId}.jpg` only. If the blob exists, verify and upsert metadata. Refuse when a deleting lease/version is set. Record `ThumbnailReadyUtc`.
5. Finalizer sets Ready only when validation, clean malware, `ThumbnailReadyUtc`, and `ModerationApprovedUtc` all match the sealed ETag, in one idempotent transaction. Avatars may skip human moderation (profile issue) but still require the clean ETag match.
6. Uncommitted-block inspector runs at least every 60 seconds for every staging key whose write SAS is unexpired, including already-Rejected rows. `Get Block List` uncommitted, sum sizes, delete the staging blob and set Rejected + `RejectedUtc` when over size or expired. Do not release the quota counter until write capability ends.
7. Committed-oversize reaper (Event Grid on blob create, poller backup ≤ 60 seconds) deletes staging blobs whose committed length exceeds the reservation and rejects the row without releasing the direct-SAS counter early.
8. Pending-expiry janitor deletes expired PendingUpload blobs and releases the counter only after SAS expiry. Quarantine hold past 7 days transitions to Rejected + `RejectedUtc`, not a hard delete.

## Contracts and invariants
- Malicious or timed-out objects are never parsed or served.
- Ready is a separate finalization step from admin approve.
- Direct-SAS quota release waits for `UploadExpiresUtc`.

## Tests
- Unit: stale ETag event does not change verdict.
- Unit: thumbnail path is deterministic and a second delivery does not create a second blob name.
- Integration or worker test: quarantine expiry sets RejectedUtc and does not delete the row.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Clean-path finalizer and stale-scan tests pass.
- [ ] Inspector/reaper/janitor are idempotent.
